title: Make It Move
prompt: Photograph the same moving thing twice: once frozen so we could count the spokes, and once blurred so we can feel it going past.
questions: Is it sharp, or is it flowing?
Did it come towards you or straight across you — and did that change the blur?
Can you hold still enough, or is there something to lean on?
Which of the two tells the better story?
technical_reminder: A slow shutter records camera shake as well as movement. Brace against a wall, a railing, or a post.
If nothing is blurring, there may simply be too much light: a larger f-number or a lower ISO will slow the shutter down.
safety_note: Photograph traffic from behind a barrier or well back from the kerb. Nobody steps into the road for a photograph.

variation.condition: If the frozen and blurred versions both worked
variation.text: Try panning: follow the moving thing with the camera as you press the shutter, so it stays sharp and the background streaks.

variation.condition: If nothing is moving fast enough
variation.text: Make the movement yourself — photograph a partner walking, running, or jumping.

review_prompt: Which photograph makes us feel the movement most?
